title: You don’t need to believe in a god to get a religious exemption from using AI at work
slides: Can you refuse AI at work and still keep your job?
US law protects religious beliefs, not just gods
Courts now accept secular 'religion' claims against AI
Employers must prove real hardship to deny exemption
Check your HR policy before your next AI mandate
thread_text:
1. Can You Refuse AI at Work?

A US court just accepted a 'secular religion' claim against an AI mandate. The employee kept their job — for now. This isn't about gods; it's about conscience.

2. Religious Freedom, Redefined

US law protects deeply held beliefs, even without a deity. Courts are now testing whether anti-AI convictions qualify under that same shield.

3. Employers Must Prove Hardship

To deny an exemption, your boss can't just say 'it's inconvenient.' They have to show real, concrete burden. That's a high bar — and a new weapon for workers.

4. The Twist: Secular Claims

A belief doesn't need a church. If you oppose AI on ethical or philosophical grounds, you might have standing. But the case law is still thin — and uneven.

5. Check Your HR Policy Today

Before your next AI mandate, read the fine print. Does your company require exemptions in writing? Ask now. Does it make sense to wait until you're forced?
